title: Food and Beverage Committed for the Event Day
content:
The food and beverage value a Private Event & Banquet Services contracted value is built on is settled by what the records show the client has committed to for the event day.

The room a confirmed booking holds is held for the whole of the event day, so an order standing on the client's corporate catering account for that day is food for that room, and the day alone settles it, whether or not the order names the room. That account is the client's Corporate Catering Service Agreement, and the orders read are those standing on its order ledger for the event's own day.

## The three cases

1. Where a confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking and catering orders stand on the client's corporate catering account for the event's own day, that value is the value the guarantee prices to together with the value of those same-day catering orders, because food ordered for that room on that day belongs to the event rather than to the catering account.
2. Where a confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking and no catering order stands for the event's own day, that value is the value the guarantee prices to alone.
3. Where no confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking, that value is the estimated contracted value standing on the booking entry.

Where no confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking, the working count the booking was taken at is not read as a guarantee in its place, and the contracted value is built on the booking entry's own estimate, with no guaranteed count to dress the room or to price a bar against.

The event's own day is the event date the confirmed guarantee entry carries, and the same-day orders are every order on the corporate catering account whose service day is that day; their values are added together.

## The same three cases as a table

| A confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking | Orders stand on the corporate catering account for the event's own day | The food and beverage value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yes | Yes | The value the guarantee prices to plus the value of those same-day orders |
| Yes | No | The value the guarantee prices to |
| No | Either way | The estimated contracted value standing on the booking entry |

## Worked illustration on hypothetical records

A booking carries a confirmed guarantee entry pricing to 18400, and the client's Corporate Catering Service Agreement carries two orders for the event's own day, of 1250 and 640. The food and beverage value is 18400 plus 1250 plus 640, that is 20290. Were there no order standing for that day, it would be 18400; and were there no confirmed guarantee entry at all, it would be the estimate standing on the booking entry, whatever the catering account showed.
